name: SLU-PP-332
used_for: A synthetic small molecule that activates the estrogen-related receptors (ERR alpha, beta and gamma), developed in academic labs and described as an exercise mimetic. It is not a peptide. Published work is in mice and cell models, where it increased exercise endurance, energy expenditure and fat oxidation and reduced fat gain. No human trials were found and no FDA approval was found.

entries.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2024 study, SLU-PP-332 was given by intraperitoneal injection at 50 mg/kg twice daily for 28 days.
entries.population: Diet-induced obese mice (and ob/ob mice for 12 days)

entries.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2023 study, SLU-PP-332 was given by intraperitoneal injection at 50 mg/kg twice daily in efficacy experiments, after a 30 mg/kg injection was used for pharmacokinetics.
Animal study only, not human data: in a 2024 heart failure study, SLU-PP-332 was given by intraperitoneal injection at 25 mg/kg twice daily.
entries.population: Mice with pressure overload-induced heart failure

internet_entries.text: A supplement-industry influencer's blog (with an affiliate discount code for a supplement containing it) lists oral SLU-PP-332 ranges of 100 to 200 mg/day as conservative, 400 mg/day as mid-range, and 600 to 800 mg/day or more as higher, and says the author personally used 400 to 800 mg for three weeks.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: A University of Florida news release says the compound is given by injection in mouse studies and that researchers hope to develop a pill, but must first refine it and test it in more animal models before human trials.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The University of Florida release says that so far the drug has not produced severe side effects in the mouse studies, with more testing needed.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: A University of Florida news release says obese mice given the compound lost about 12% of body weight over one month without eating less, and normal mice ran about 70% longer and 45% farther.
Wikipedia describes SLU-PP-332 as a potent but non-selective ERR agonist, lists only mouse data, and gives no human clinical data or safety information.

research.summary: Identification of SLU-PP-332 as a pan-ERR agonist (highest potency at ERR alpha) tested in muscle cells and mice.
research.finding: Increased mitochondrial function in muscle cells and, in mice, oxidative muscle fibers and exercise endurance; effects depended on ERR alpha.

research.summary: Study of SLU-PP-332 in diet-induced obese and ob/ob mice.
research.finding: Increased energy expenditure and fatty acid oxidation, decreased fat mass gain and improved insulin sensitivity in mice.

research.summary: Mouse study of pan-ERR agonists, including SLU-PP-332, in heart failure models.
research.finding: In a mouse pressure-overload heart failure model, SLU-PP-332 and SLU-PP-915 improved ejection fraction, reduced fibrosis and increased survival, with activation of fatty acid metabolism and mitochondrial genes.

research.summary: Analytical and in vitro human liver metabolism study of SLU-PP-332 and SLU-PP-915 for sports drug testing.
research.finding: Identified nine in vitro metabolites of SLU-PP-332; describes the compounds as investigational exercise mimetics with doping potential.

dose.summary: No human dose exists. In mice, the studies used injections of 25 to 50 mg per kilogram of body weight (mg/kg) of this small molecule, which is not a peptide. Online sources describe human doses that differ widely, from under 1 milligram (mg) to hundreds of mg a day, and none are backed by a study.

items.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2024 study, SLU-PP-332 was given by intraperitoneal (into the abdominal cavity) injection at 50 mg/kg twice daily for 28 days in diet-induced obese mice (and ob/ob mice for 12 days).

items.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2023 study, SLU-PP-332 was given to mice by intraperitoneal injection at 50 mg/kg twice daily in efficacy experiments, after a 30 mg/kg injection was used for pharmacokinetics (how the body handles the drug).

items.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2024 heart failure study, SLU-PP-332 was given by intraperitoneal injection at 25 mg/kg twice daily to mice with pressure overload-induced heart failure.

items.text: Peptide Initiative, an educational database, suggests 0.5 to 1 mg once daily by subcutaneous injection, and mentions oral use as an alternative. It says no human trials exist.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptibase, a peptide seller, says the commonly used oral dose is 250 micrograms (mcg) to 1 mg daily, with a range up to 1.5 mg, and that people start low and increase. It cites no human studies.

timing.summary: No study has tested time of day in animals or people. Two online sources suggest morning dosing, which is untested.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says morning dosing is recommended to match the body's metabolic rhythm, that it can be split between morning and early afternoon, and that people who exercise can take it 30 to 60 minutes beforehand. This is not backed by a study.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptibase, a peptide seller, says to take it in the morning or split between morning and afternoon, and that metabolic effects begin about 2 hours after a dose. It cites no study for this.
items.label: internet

fasting.summary: No food study exists for this compound. One online educational site says it can be taken with or without food, and one says no food rule applies.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says it can be taken with or without food, and that some users take it with a light meal to ease possible stomach upset. This is untested.
items.label: internet

items.text: Biomogging, a site with affiliate links to peptide sellers, says no specific food requirement applies. This is untested.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: In mice, the studies gave the compound twice daily. Online sources suggest once or twice daily in people, which has not been studied.

items.text: In the 2024 obesity study, SLU-PP-332 was injected twice daily in obese mice. The 2023 and 2024 heart failure studies also used twice-daily injections in mice.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptibase, a peptide seller, says to take it 1 to 2 times daily.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Initiative says to take it once daily.
items.label: internet

items.text: Biomogging, a site with affiliate links to peptide sellers, says to split subcutaneous doses between morning and afternoon to copy the twice-daily mouse dosing.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Mouse studies ran from 12 days to about a month. Nothing is known about longer use or about stopping in any species. Online sources suggest cycles of 4 to 12 weeks, which are untested.

items.text: Animal study only, not human data: SLU-PP-332 was given twice daily for 28 days to diet-induced obese mice and for 12 days to ob/ob mice. The study did not report what happened after stopping.
items.label: research

items.text: The University of Florida news release says the obese mice received the drug twice a day for a month.

items.text: Peptide Initiative lists 8 to 12 weeks for research use.
items.label: internet

storage_and_handling.summary: No manufacturer or regulator storage rules exist because there is no human product. Online sources give conflicting storage advice, which is untested.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says to keep powder or tablets at room temperature (15 to 25 degrees C) away from sunlight, and to refrigerate reconstituted product at 2 to 8 degrees C and never freeze it.
items.label: internet

items.text: Biomogging, a site with affiliate links to peptide sellers, says to store it at 2 to 8 degrees C, that it does not dissolve in water so an oil or DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) vehicle is needed, and to rotate injection sites. This is untested.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: It activates the estrogen-related receptors (ERRs), proteins that regulate how cells make energy, with the strongest effect on ERR alpha. This is known from cell and mouse work only.

items.text: SLU-PP-332 targets all three ERRs but is most potent at ERR alpha. In mouse muscle cells it increased mitochondrial function (the cell's energy-making machinery), and the endurance effect in mice depended on ERR alpha. This is animal and cell evidence.
items.label: research

items.text: In a mouse heart failure model, ERR gamma was the main mediator of the heart-protecting effect, with increased fatty acid use and mitochondrial genes. Animal evidence only.
items.label: research

items.text: In a test-tube study with human liver preparations, nine metabolites (breakdown products) of SLU-PP-332 were identified. How the body handles it in people is not known.
items.label: research

items.text: Wikipedia describes it as a potent but non-selective ERR agonist, strongest at ERR alpha with a potency (EC50) of 98 nanomolar.
items.label: internet

items.text: Superpower, a health testing company that offers peptide access, says it has poor oral bioavailability (little reaches the blood when swallowed) and that its behavior in humans is unknown.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: In mice only, it raised exercise endurance, energy use and fat burning, and limited fat gain. No human trial exists.

items.text: In obese and ob/ob mice, SLU-PP-332 increased energy expenditure and fatty acid oxidation, decreased fat mass gain and improved insulin sensitivity.
items.label: research

items.text: In mice, it increased oxidative muscle fibers and exercise endurance.
items.label: research

items.text: In mice with pressure overload heart failure, it improved ejection fraction, reduced fibrosis and increased survival.
